779	netqueue takes FILE QUEUES DATA and performs deterministic multi-hop
780	store-and-forward over the metric topology (cost, bandwidth, latency,
781	up; parsed strictly like metric's FILE). QUEUES is a JSON array of
782	[from,to,capacity] triples that covers every directed FILE link
783	exactly once (capacity a non-boolean integer in 1..MAX_COST; an unknown
784	or self pair, a duplicate, or a missing/extra pair is code 5). DATA is
785	a JSON array, possibly empty, of [id,time,source,destination,size]:
786	id is a 1..256 codepoint UTF-8 string unique within DATA, time a
787	non-boolean integer in 0..MAX_TIME non-decreasing in array order,
788	source/destination FILE nodes, size a non-boolean integer in
789	1..MAX_COST. A route is the lowest-cost up-only path with ties broken
790	by the Unicode node sequence, one Dijkstra per distinct source; a
791	packet with source == destination delivers immediately at its
792	injection time, and an unreachable destination is reported without
793	entering any queue. Each link is a non-preemptive FIFO: a packet asks
794	for capacity on whole arrival, occupies it while waiting and sending,
795	and releases it at send completion; sending takes
796	ceil(size/bandwidth) and reception follows latency units later, and an
797	admission exceeding capacity ends the packet as overflow on that link,
798	occupying and enqueuing nothing. At each distinct time, repeatedly
799	until stable: completions release capacity, then receptions and fresh
800	injections due at the time are handled in DATA order (merged by packet
801	index), then every idle link with a queued head starts it once in FILE
802	order. A computed time above MAX_TIME is code 5 with no partial
803	output. Result top-level key order is packets,links. Each packet row is
804	[id,status,path,finish,delay,dropLink,hops] in DATA order: status is
805	delivered, unreachable, or overflow; path is the full node list (an
806	empty list for unreachable); finish is the completion time, delay
807	finish-injection, dropLink the [from,to] that overflowed (null
808	otherwise); unreachable rows have null finish/delay/dropLink and no
809	hops, and an overflow hop carries its arrive with the remaining fields
810	null. hops lists, per traversed link in order, objects with key order

netqueue takes FILE QUEUES DATA and performs deterministic multi-hop
store-and-forward over the metric topology (cost, bandwidth, latency,
up; parsed strictly like metric's FILE). QUEUES is a JSON array of
[from,to,capacity] triples that covers every directed FILE link
exactly once (capacity a non-boolean integer in 1..MAX_COST; an unknown
or self pair, a duplicate, or a missing/extra pair is code 5). DATA is
a JSON array, possibly empty, of [id,time,source,destination,size]:
id is a 1..256 codepoint UTF-8 string unique within DATA, time a
non-boolean integer in 0..MAX_TIME non-decreasing in array order,
source/destination FILE nodes, size a non-boolean integer in
1..MAX_COST. A route is the lowest-cost up-only path with ties broken
by the Unicode node sequence, one Dijkstra per distinct source; a
packet with source == destination delivers immediately at its
injection time, and an unreachable destination is reported without
entering any queue. Each link is a non-preemptive FIFO: a packet asks
for capacity on whole arrival, occupies it while waiting and sending,
and releases it at send completion; sending takes
ceil(size/bandwidth) and reception follows latency units later, and an
admission exceeding capacity ends the packet as overflow on that link,
occupying and enqueuing nothing. At each distinct time, repeatedly
until stable: completions release capacity, then receptions and fresh
injections due at the time are handled in DATA order (merged by packet
index), then every idle link with a queued head starts it once in FILE
order. A computed time above MAX_TIME is code 5 with no partial
output. Result top-level key order is packets,links. Each packet row is
[id,status,path,finish,delay,dropLink,hops] in DATA order: status is
delivered, unreachable, or overflow; path is the full node list (an
empty list for unreachable); finish is the completion time, delay
finish-injection, dropLink the [from,to] that overflowed (null
otherwise); unreachable rows have null finish/delay/dropLink and no
hops, and an overflow hop carries its arrive with the remaining fields
null. hops lists, per traversed link in order, objects with key order
from,to,arrive,start,depart,receive,wait (arrive the whole-arrival
time, start/depart the FIFO send interval, receive depart+latency,
wait start-arrive). links follows FILE order as
[from,to,enqueued,overflow,peak,lastDepart]: enqueued counts successful
admissions, overflow the failed ones, peak the highest simultaneous
occupancy, and lastDepart the last send completion time (0 for a link
that never sent). Worst case is O(S((V+E) log V) + H log(P+E)) for S
distinct sources and H actual hops, with O(V+E+P+H) extra space.
netshape is read-only and takes FILE SHAPERS DATA, applying tbucket's
token bucket to netqueue's deterministic multi-hop store-and-forward
while keeping netqueue's entry behavior. FILE is metric's topology
parsed exactly like netqueue's. SHAPERS is a JSON array of
[from,to,rate,burst,capacity] quintuples covering every directed FILE
link exactly once (an unknown or self pair, a duplicate, or a
missing/extra pair is code 5); rate, burst, and capacity are
non-boolean integers in 1..MAX_COST. DATA follows netqueue's exact
[id,time,source,destination,size] contract, including unique ids and
the empty-array case. Each link starts clock 0 with burst tokens and
refills at rate per elapsed unit capped at burst; starting a send
deducts the head's size. A packet whose size exceeds burst ends as
oversize on arrival, consuming no tokens and occupying no capacity;
any other packet whose admission would take occupied bytes plus size
past capacity ends as overflow there instead. An admitted packet holds
its bytes from admission through send completion. An idle link serves
only its FIFO head; when tokens cannot cover the head it waits until
the first integer time with enough tokens, the send then takes
ceil(size/bandwidth) and reception follows latency units later.
Routing (one lowest-cost Dijkstra per distinct source with the
Unicode node sequence tie-break), source == destination delivery, and
unreachable handling reuse netqueue verbatim. At each distinct time,
repeatedly until stable, send completions release first, then
receptions and fresh injections due at the time are admitted in DATA
order (merged by packet index), and finally each idle link whose head
is now token-covered starts it once in FILE order; token-ready
deadlines at the time join this final pass and zero-latency work
repeats the instant. A computed time above MAX_TIME is code 5 with no
partial output. Result top-level key order is packets,links. Packet
rows are [id,status,path,finish,delay,dropLink,hops] in DATA order:
status is delivered, unreachable, oversize, or overflow; hops and the
null conventions follow netqueue exactly (an oversize or overflow hop
carries only its arrive), and dropLink is the offending [from,to].

[from,to,enqueued,oversize,overflow,peak,lastDepart]: enqueued counts
successful admissions, oversize and overflow the failed ones, peak

Now let me check the "flow" length validation: dispatch flow uses `1 <= len(value) <= MAX_FLOW_LEN` where len is Python str len = Unicode code points. The task says "1 至 256 个 Unicode 码点的 flow" — 1..256 Unicode codepoints. netqueue id also 1..256. In dispatch they also call `.encode("utf-8")` — why? To reject lone surrogates (Python strings can contain surrogates which can't be encoded UTF-8). I'll mirror that for id and flow.

Now let me understand the exact semantics fully.

**ecmpqueue design:**

Input args: `ecmpqueue FILE QUEUES MODE DATA` → 6 argv total (relay.py + 5 args).

- FILE: netqueue rules → `load_network(file_path, metrics=True, strict=True)`
- QUEUES: netqueue exact parsing
- MODE: "flow" or "packet" else fail(5)
- DATA: JSON array, may be empty. Each item: [id, flow, time, source, destination, size] (6 elements).
  - id: 1..256 codepoint UTF-8 string, unique
  - flow: 1..256 codepoint UTF-8 string (may repeat)
  - time: non-boolean int 0..MAX_TIME, non-decreasing
  - source, destination: FILE nodes
  - size: non-boolean int 1..MAX_COST

**Routing at injection:** static up topology (initial FILE up flags; no events). For each source-destination pair, per dispatch semantics:
- lowest total cost
- candidate first hops: deduplicated, sorted by Unicode codepoint order
- representative path per first hop: lexicographically smallest node sequence (per `dispatch_candidates`).

flow mode: SHA-256 of compact JSON array [flow,source,destination], first 8 bytes big-endian integer mod candidate count. Same endpoint pair + same flow always same path.

packet mode: independent cursor per endpoint pair; only on reachable non-zero-hop packets, polled in DATA order. So each (source, destination) pair has its own round-robin cursor starting at 0; only packets that are reachable with ≥1 hop advance the cursor. def compute_ecmpqueue(nodes, links, cap_of, mode, packets):
    # dispatch candidate selection combined with netqueue's deterministic
    # multi-hop FIFO clock on one static up topology. Every packet chooses
    # its complete path once at injection time and is never rerouted:
    # congestion can end it as overflow but never changes the route.
    #
    # Candidates come from dispatch_candidates once per distinct
    # source/destination pair: lowest total cost, candidate first hops
    # deduplicated and sorted by Unicode code point, each with its
    # lexicographically smallest representative path. flow mode selects
    # with the first eight SHA-256 bytes of compact [flow,source,
    # destination] modulo the candidate count, so a flow on a pair always
    # takes the same hop. packet mode keeps one cursor per pair and
    # round-robins reachable nonzero-hop packets in DATA order; source ==
    # destination packets deliver immediately and neither hash nor cursor
    # advances for them, and a pair with no candidate is unreachable.
    #
    # The clock, capacity accounting, FIFO, ceil(size/bandwidth) send,
    # latency reception, overflow, same-instant phase order, and MAX_TIME
    # rule are netqueue's verbatim; only the route selection differs.
    n = len(packets)

    # One candidate computation per distinct pair, cached for all of its
    # packets. Each entry is (hops, rep_paths), None for unreachable.
    candidates = {}
    for _, _, _, source, destination, _ in packets:
        if source == destination:
            continue
        pair = (source, destination)
        if pair not in candidates:
            total, hops, rep_paths = dispatch_candidates(
                nodes, links, source, destination)
            candidates[pair] = None if total is None else (hops, rep_paths)

    # Per-packet chosen path; None marks a packet that never enters the
    # clock (immediate delivery or unreachable), exactly like netqueue.
    paths = [None] * n
    flow_hash_cache = {}
    pair_cursor = {}
    # results[i] = [id, flow, status, nextHops, selectedNextHop, path,
    #               finish, delay, dropLink, hops]
    results = [[pid, flow, None, None, None, None, None, None, None, []]
               for pid, flow, _, _, _, _ in packets]

    # Select routes in DATA order: packet mode's per-pair cursor advances
    # solely with the DATA position of reachable nonzero-hop packets.
    for i, (_, flow, ptime, source, destination, _) in enumerate(packets):
        if source == destination:
            results[i][2] = "delivered"
            results[i][3] = [source]
            results[i][4] = source
            results[i][5] = [source]
            results[i][6] = ptime
            results[i][7] = 0
            continue
        cand = candidates[(source, destination)]
        if cand is None:
            results[i][2] = "unreachable"
            results[i][3] = []
            results[i][4] = None
            results[i][5] = []
            continue
        hops, rep_paths = cand
        if mode == "flow":
            key_pair = (source, destination, flow)
            index = flow_hash_cache.get(key_pair)
            if index is None:
                key = json.dumps([flow, source, destination],
                                 ensure_ascii=False,
                                 separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
                digest = hashlib.sha256(key).digest()
                index = int.from_bytes(digest[:8], "big") % len(hops)
                flow_hash_cache[key_pair] = index
        else:
            index = pair_cursor.get((source, destination), 0)
            pair_cursor[(source, destination)] = index + 1
            index %= len(hops)
        paths[i] = rep_paths[index]
        results[i][3] = hops
        results[i][4] = hops[index]
        results[i][5] = rep_paths[index]

    E = len(links)
    link_index = {}
    for i, link in enumerate(links):
        link_index[(link["from"], link["to"])] = i
    bw = [l["bandwidth"] for l in links]
    lat = [l["latency"] for l in links]
    cap = [cap_of[i] for i in range(E)]
    occupancy = [0] * E
    queues = [deque() for _ in range(E)]   # admitted packet indices
    busy = [False] * E
    admitted = [0] * E
    overflows = [0] * E
    peak = [0] * E
    last_depart = [0] * E

    # hop_at[i] is the link index of the hop the packet is about to cross.
    hop_at = [0] * n

    def check_time(value):
        if value > MAX_TIME:
            fail(5)
        return value

    completion_heap = []
    reception_heap = []
    idle_heap = []

    def admit(i, now):
        # Packet i is whole at its hop_at[i] link: test capacity once.
        path = paths[i]
        k = hop_at[i]
        frm, to = path[k], path[k + 1]
        li = link_index[(frm, to)]
        hop = {"from": frm, "to": to, "arrive": now, "start": None,
               "depart": None, "receive": None, "wait": None}
        results[i][9].append(hop)
        size = packets[i][5]
        if occupancy[li] + size > cap[li]:
            results[i][2] = "overflow"
            results[i][8] = [frm, to]
            overflows[li] += 1
            return
        occupancy[li] += size
        if occupancy[li] > peak[li]:
            peak[li] = occupancy[li]
        admitted[li] += 1
        queues[li].append(i)
        if not busy[li]:
            heapq.heappush(idle_heap, li)

    def release(now, i, li):
        # Waiting and sending both held these bytes until now.
        occupancy[li] -= packets[i][5]
        busy[li] = False
        last_depart[li] = now
        if queues[li]:
            heapq.heappush(idle_heap, li)
        receive = check_time(now + lat[li])
        results[i][9][-1]["receive"] = receive
        path = paths[i]
        if hop_at[i] + 1 == len(path) - 1:
            results[i][2] = "delivered"
            results[i][6] = receive
            results[i][7] = receive - packets[i][2]
        else:
            hop_at[i] += 1
            heapq.heappush(reception_heap, (receive, i))

    def start_heads(now):
        # One FILE-order pass; each link starts at most its single head.
        while idle_heap:
            li = heapq.heappop(idle_heap)
            if busy[li] or not queues[li]:
                continue
            i = queues[li].popleft()
            size = packets[i][5]
            depart = check_time(now + (size + bw[li] - 1) // bw[li])
            busy[li] = True
            hop = results[i][9][-1]
            hop["start"] = now
            hop["depart"] = depart
            hop["wait"] = now - hop["arrive"]
            heapq.heappush(completion_heap, (depart, li, i))

    inject_at = 0

    def prime_inject():
        j = inject_at
        while j < n and paths[j] is None:
            j += 1
        return packets[j][2] if j < n else None

    def advance_inject(now):
        # Consume every entry with injection time <= now, return the
        # routed ones in DATA order, and skip unrouted entries. O(P) over
        # the whole run.
        nonlocal inject_at
        due_list = []
        while inject_at < n and packets[inject_at][2] <= now:
            if paths[inject_at] is not None:
                due_list.append(inject_at)
            inject_at += 1
        return due_list

    next_inject = prime_inject()

    def next_time():
        t = next_inject
        if completion_heap:
            ct = completion_heap[0][0]
            if t is None or ct < t:
                t = ct
        if reception_heap:
            rt = reception_heap[0][0]
            if t is None or rt < t:
                t = rt
        return t

    while True:
        now = next_time()
        if now is None:
            break
        check_time(now)
        # netqueue's fixed phase order, repeated until the instant is
        # stable: zero-latency receptions feed the next round.
        moved = True
        while moved:
            moved = False
            while completion_heap and completion_heap[0][0] == now:
                _, li, i = heapq.heappop(completion_heap)
                release(now, i, li)
                moved = True
            due = []
            while reception_heap and reception_heap[0][0] == now:
                _, i = heapq.heappop(reception_heap)
                due.append(i)
            injected = advance_inject(now)
            next_inject = prime_inject()
            a = b = 0
            while a < len(due) or b < len(injected):
                if b >= len(injected) or (a < len(due)
                                          and due[a] < injected[b]):
                    admit(due[a], now)
                    a += 1
                else:
                    admit(injected[b], now)
                    b += 1
            if due or injected:
                moved = True
            if idle_heap:
                start_heads(now)
                moved = True

    return {"packets": results,
            "links": [[links[i]["from"], links[i]["to"], admitted[i],
                       overflows[i], peak[i], last_depart[i]]
                      for i in range(E)]}

# lexicographically smallest representative path. flow mode selects
    # with the first eight SHA-256 bytes of compact [flow,source,
    # destination] modulo the candidate count, so a flow on a pair always
    # takes the same hop. packet mode keeps one cursor per pair and
    # round-robins reachable nonzero-hop packets in DATA order; source ==
    # destination packets deliver immediately and neither hash nor cursor
    # advances for them, and a pair with no candidate is unreachable.
    #
    # The clock, capacity accounting, FIFO, ceil(size/bandwidth) send,
    # latency reception, overflow, same-instant phase order, and MAX_TIME
    # rule are netqueue's verbatim; only the route selection differs.
    n = len(packets)

    # One candidate computation per distinct pair, cached for all of its
    # packets. Each entry is (hops, rep_paths), None for unreachable.
    candidates = {}
    for _, _, _, source, destination, _ in packets:
        if source == destination:
            continue
        pair = (source, destination)
        if pair not in candidates:
            total, hops, rep_paths = dispatch_candidates(
                nodes, links, source, destination)
            candidates[pair] = None if total is None else (hops, rep_paths)

    # Per-packet chosen path; None marks a packet that never enters the
    # clock (immediate delivery or unreachable), exactly like netqueue.
    paths = [None] * n
    flow_hash_cache = {}
    pair_cursor = {}
    # results[i] = [id, flow, status, nextHops, selectedNextHop, path,
    #               finish, delay, dropLink, hops]
    results = [[pid, flow, None, None, None, None, None, None, None, []]
               for pid, flow, _, _, _, _ in packets]

    # Select routes in DATA order: packet mode's per-pair cursor advances
    # solely with the DATA position of reachable nonzero-hop packets.
    for i, (_, flow, ptime, source, destination, _) in enumerate(packets):
        if source == destination:
            results[i][2] = "delivered"
            results[i][3] = [source]
            results[i][4] = source
            results[i][5] = [source]
            results[i][6] = ptime
            results[i][7] = 0
            continue
        cand = candidates[(source, destination)]
        if cand is None:
            results[i][2] = "unreachable"
            results[i][3] = []
            results[i][4] = None
            results[i][5] = []
            continue
        hops, rep_paths = cand
        if mode == "flow":
            key_pair = (source, destination, flow)
            index = flow_hash_cache.get(key_pair)
            if index is None:
                key = json.dumps([flow, source, destination],
                                 ensure_ascii=False,
                                 separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
                digest = hashlib.sha256(key).digest()
                index = int.from_bytes(digest[:8], "big") % len(hops)
                flow_hash_cache[key_pair] = index
        else:
            index = pair_cursor.get((source, destination), 0)
            pair_cursor[(source, destination)] = index + 1
            index %= len(hops)
        paths[i] = rep_paths[index]
        results[i][3] = hops
        results[i][4] = hops[index]
        results[i][5] = rep_paths[index]

    E = len(links)
    link_index = {}
    for i, link in enumerate(links):
        link_index[(link["from"], link["to"])] = i
    bw = [l["bandwidth"] for l in links]
    lat = [l["latency"] for l in links]
    cap = [cap_of[i] for i in range(E)]
    occupancy = [0] * E
    queues = [deque() for _ in range(E)]   # admitted packet indices
    busy = [False] * E
    admitted = [0] * E
    overflows = [0] * E
    peak = [0] * E
    last_depart = [0] * E

    # hop_at[i] is the link index of the hop the packet is about to cross.
    hop_at = [0] * n

    def check_time(value):
        if value > MAX_TIME:
            fail(5)
        return value

    completion_heap = []
    reception_heap = []
    idle_heap = []

    def admit(i, now):
        # Packet i is whole at its hop_at[i] link: test capacity once.
        path = paths[i]
        k = hop_at[i]
        frm, to = path[k], path[k + 1]
        li = link_index[(frm, to)]
        hop = {"from": frm, "to": to, "arrive": now, "start": None,
               "depart": None, "receive": None, "wait": None}
        results[i][9].append(hop)
        size = packets[i][5]
        if occupancy[li] + size > cap[li]:
            results[i][2] = "overflow"
            results[i][8] = [frm, to]
            overflows[li] += 1
            return

content.text:
Done. I added a new read-only `ecmpqueue` entry point to `relay.py`, leaving all existing entries untouched.

## What was added

**`compute_ecmpqueue(nodes, links, cap_of, mode, packets)`** (after `compute_netqueue`, relay.py:2881)
- **Routing at injection, once per packet** over the static up topology via the existing `dispatch_candidates`: lowest total cost, first hops deduplicated/sorted by Unicode code point, each with its lexicographically smallest representative path.
- **flow mode** — SHA-256 of compact `[flow,source,destination]` JSON, first 8 bytes as big-endian int mod candidate count (cached per pair+flow); same flow on a pair always takes the same path.
- **packet mode** — one cursor per endpoint pair, advancing only on reachable non-zero-hop packets in DATA order; source==destination packets deliver immediately (`finish = injection`, `delay = 0`) without advancing, and candidate-less pairs report `unreachable`.
- **The clock is netqueue's verbatim** — capacity occupancy, non-preemptive FIFO, `ceil(size/bandwidth)` sends, latency reception, overflow (single capacity test, no enqueue), and the complete→receive/inject-merge-by-DATA-index→idle-link-start phase order repeated to stability, including the MAX_TIME → exit 5 rule. Congestion never reroutes.

**CLI handler** (`ecmpqueue FILE QUEUES MODE DATA`, 6 args): FILE/QUEUES parsed exactly like netqueue (strict metric topology, 1:1 queue coverage); MODE must be `flow`/`packet`; DATA items are 6-tuples `[id,flow,time,source,destination,size]` with unique ids, 1–256 codepoint flow/id, non-decreasing times. Failures exit 2/3/4/5 with empty stdout; success emits compact UTF-8 JSON + LF via the existing shared output path. Output key order is `packets,links`; packet rows are `[id,flow,status,nextHops,selectedNextHop,path,finish,delay,dropLink,hops]`, links `[from,to,enqueued,overflow,peak,lastDepart]` in FILE order.

**Docs** — added the usage line, a full spec paragraph, and extended the exit-code-4 sentence to name `ecmpqueue`.

## Verification
- Packet round-robin (A,B,A…) and per-pair independent cursors; self/unreachable packets don't advance cursors.
- Flow selection matches the `dispatch` command byte-for-byte; Unicode flow/node hashing verified independently with raw non-ASCII-escaped output.
- On a single-path topology, packet rows and link counters are exactly netqueue's output (field remap); overflow at mid-path keeps the static route and a congested preferred path is never rerouted.
- Brute-force path enumeration parity for both modes (multi-hop candidates, unreachable pairs, self pairs) over a random topology; `enqueued + overflow == hop records`.
- All 21 error cases return the right code with empty stdout; empty DATA, determinism, and regression smoke on `netqueue`/`dispatch` pass; `py_compile` clean.

One judgment call worth flagging: the spec doesn't spell out `nextHops`/`selectedNextHop` for a zero-hop source==destination row. I used `[source]`/`source`, mirroring `compute_ecmp`'s self-route convention (`nextHops:[source]`, `selectedNextHop:source`) — easy to change if your reference expects different nulls.
